definitions.explanation: Expresses strong confidence that something will happen or is true. Used when the speaker feels certain about a prediction or expectation.

examples.japanese: ⟦{明日|あした}→明日：00501_ashita⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧きっと⟦{晴|は}れます→晴れる：00701_hareru⟧⟦よ→よ：09475_yo⟧。
examples.english: It will surely be sunny tomorrow.

examples.japanese: きっと⟦{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}→大丈夫：00772_daijoubu⟧⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧⟦よ→よ：09475_yo⟧。
examples.english: I'm sure it will be fine.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧きっと⟦{来|き}ます→来る：00254_kuru⟧。
きっと⟦{上手|じょうず}→上手：00707_jouzu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なります→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦よ→よ：09475_yo⟧。⟦{頑張|がんば}って→頑張る：01222_ganbaru⟧⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: You'll surely get good at it. Keep trying.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼女|かのじょ}→彼女：01286_kanojo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧きっと⟦{私|わたし}→私：02988_watashi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦こと→こと：01164_koto⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{忘|わす}れていない→忘れる：00474_wasureru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{思|おも}います→思う：00492_omou⟧。
examples.english: I think she surely hasn't forgotten about me.

notes:
きっと expresses the speaker's strong confidence that something will happen or is true.

DEGREES OF CERTAINTY:
- きっと: surely, definitely (~90% confidence)
- たぶん: probably (~70% confidence)
- もしかしたら: perhaps, maybe (~30% confidence)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- きっと〜だろう: surely ~ (with conjecture)
- きっと〜と{思|おも}う: I'm sure that ~
- きっと〜はず: surely must be ~
- きっと{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}: I'm sure it'll be fine

USAGE:
Often used to encourage or reassure others. Works with both positive and negative predictions. Usually written in hiragana.

NOTE:
きっと expresses the speaker's subjective confidence. For objective certainty, use {必|かなら}ず (without fail) or {確|たし}かに (certainly).
